title: It's voting day in Yellowknife. Here's what you should know
summary: Today is voting day for the Yellowknife municipal elections, as well as the trustee elections for two school boards in the city.

image.caption: A sign for advance voting, which began Oct. 5. Twenty-one candidates are running for eight city council seats, while two candidates are running for mayor. (Carson Asmundson/CBC)

blocks.text: Today is voting day for the Yellowknife municipal elections, as well as the trustee elections for two school boards in the city.
5 voting stations open across the city from 10 a.m. to 7 p.m.
Voters in Yellowknife will be selecting a new mayor and council Monday, as well as trustees for school boards.
On Monday night, CBC North will be running a live page where you can follow the results, news and analysis. Reporters will be in the field talking to candidates throughout the night.
There are 21 candidates running for city council, of which the top eight will be elected, and two running for mayor.

blocks.text: There are five voting stations open Monday from 10 a.m. until 7 p.m. These include École Įtłʼǫ̀, Range Lake North School, the Tree of Peace Friendship Centre, Weledeh Catholic School and the Multiplex.
People can vote at any of the stations.
The city is offering free transit to voting stations Monday and extending transit hours for the election.
You can read more about the candidates running for Yellowknife District 1 and the Yellowknife Catholic Schools.
You can also learn more about the school trustees' role here.
Downtown revitalization, housing and navigating the economy especially with potential forthcoming military investment have been big topics this time around.
Luke Carroll is a journalist with CBC News in Yellowknife. He can be reached at luke.carroll@cbc.ca.
